That is with every regime's growth spread × 1.5, the one number fitted on these outcomes (and used here): as the hidden Markov model estimates them, the range held 68% (18% below, 14% above) — a single year's regime spread understates how far revenue can drift over several.

steps: S = the expansion in year 5: the revenue it adds $49.44B (to $74.20B) × margin 6.4% × (1 − tax), as a growing perpetuity, discounted = $24.49B
K = capital to build it: $49.44B ÷ sales-to-capital 1.60 = $30.93B
σ = 35% (its stock, a year of daily closes), T = 5 years, r = 4.91% → C = $7.58B
assets in place = NOPAT $1.03B ÷ WACC = $13.73B; value = ($13.73B + $7.58B − net debt $5.91B) ÷ 275,400,000 = $55.93

methods.fit: It is loss-making or growing fast: much of its value is the chance to become a larger, profitable business, which behaves like an option — worth more the more uncertain it is.

methods.formula: Value = D₀ × [(1 + g_L) + H × (g_S − g_L)] ÷ (kₑ − g_L);  growth falls in a straight line from g_S to g_L over 2H years
inputs: SEC 10-K / 10-Q, diluted shares (the main site's reading)

methods.fit: It pays a dividend whose growth is likely to slow from today's pace to the economy's, which the H-model spreads over ten years.
